label: Population 2025 (log10)
rationale: Market size floor: every therapy needs patients. Log because attractiveness scales sub-linearly with raw population. Chronic weighted lower than acute: chronic value concentrates in diagnosed/affluent sub-pools rather than headcount. v1.3: current GHS-POP 2025 replaces census pop2011 (15 years stale + verified errors: Aizawl 37k vs 400k census, Sikar 1.69M vs 2.68M, Delhi pre-2012 layout); same switch applied to every per-100k denominator.

label: Population density (per sq km)
rationale: Concentration makes patients reachable per rep-visit and accelerates infectious transmission. Core acute variable (episodic illness spreads with crowding); mild chronic relevance.

label: Population under 15 (%)
rationale: Paediatric pool drives acute demand (antibiotics ORS antipyretics vaccines). Zero chronic weight: chronic therapies target adults; NFHS 2019-21 vintage beats Census u6 share.

label: Recent in-migrants per 1000 (last residence outside district)
rationale: The floating-population / medical-catchment proxy the framework previously lacked (official Census D-02): in-migrants whose last residence was OUTSIDE the district (other districts of the state + other states + abroad), duration <10y at census. Migration magnets carry transient patient pools that lean on episodic first-contact care and pharmacy channels (no local chronic-care relationship yet), and in-migration is revealed economic pull. Acute > chronic. 2011 stock (same vintage class as the SECC shares) per CURRENT resident - the dilution in fast-growing districts makes it conservative; intra-district moves excluded by construction. Extension path: swap in mobility data when a non-scraped source exists.

label: Diabetes prevalence (% adults)
rationale: Directly measured blood-sugar burden = anti-diabetic market. Repeat-prescription anchor therapy for chronic pharma; men+women averaged for a district adult rate.

label: Hypertension prevalence (% adults)
rationale: Measured elevated-BP burden = anti-hypertensive/cardiac market; the largest chronic category in Indian pharma (IPM). Same construction as diabetes.

label: Obesity (women BMI 25+ %)
rationale: Metabolic-syndrome upstream risk: predicts future diabetes/CVD therapy starts. Only women measured consistently across NFHS rounds.

label: Central obesity (women high-risk WHR >0.85 %)
rationale: The LIFESTYLE-driven metabolic-risk signal distinct from BMI. NFHS-5 indicator #80 (women with high-risk waist-to-hip ratio >0.85) - a NEW NFHS-5 measurement (not in NFHS-4), capturing CENTRAL/abdominal adiposity. For South Asians this is the WHO-endorsed 'thin-fat phenotype' marker: it predicts type-2 diabetes / CVD / dyslipidaemia therapy demand BETTER than BMI, and captures the large pool of normal-BMI-but-abdominally-obese Indians that obese_women_pct (#79, BMI>=25) misses. Redundancy gate: max |rho| vs any scored feature is only 0.17 (anaemia, negative), and just +0.09 vs BMI-obesity itself - the cleanest gate pass in the registry, confirming it measures a genuinely orthogonal dimension of chronic latent need rather than re-counting the obesity already carried. Chronic-only (w 2/3/0): a metabolic risk factor for chronic NCD demand, not an acute first-contact market. Weight 3 (risk-factor tier, matching tobacco_use_pct - not the 4-5 of measured disease): it is an upstream modifiable-risk leading indicator, and its near-zero cross-sectional correlation with measured diabetes prevalence (+0.06) is expected for a true risk factor decoupled from diagnosis/access confounding - additive precisely because of that independence, but held at a moderate weight against the known measurement noise in survey waist/hip anthropometry (median 58% high-risk is a broad cut). Direction +: more central obesity = larger future diabetes/CVD patient pool = more chronic latent need. 705/785 observed (full NFHS-5 direct coverage; remainder reach the imputation ladder). Added v1.4.14.

label: Tobacco use (% adults)
rationale: Risk factor for COPD/CVD/oncology therapy demand; leading indicator rather than diagnosed demand hence moderate weight.

label: Alcohol use (% adults)
rationale: Hepatic/GI/psychiatric burden risk factor; weaker and socially under-reported hence low weight.

label: Anaemia in women (%)
rationale: Iron-therapy and gynae-supplement market; sits between chronic (sustained supplementation) and acute (IV iron severe cases) so weighted in both.

label: Diabetes OPD visits per 1000
rationale: Revealed DIAGNOSED diabetic demand in public OPD - burden that already reaches care. Complements NFHS prevalence (need) with treatment-seeking (demand). Chronic core.

label: Hypertension OPD visits per 1000
rationale: Revealed diagnosed hypertensive demand; same logic as diabetes OPD.

label: Neuro/psych OPD per 1000 (stroke+mental+epilepsy)
rationale: CNS chronic therapy demand (anti-epileptics antidepressants post-stroke care) - a fast-growing chronic segment. Summed: single CNS demand signal, components too sparse alone.

label: Ophthalmic OPD per 1000
rationale: Chronic eye-care demand (glaucoma dry-eye diabetic retinopathy); also cataract surgical load marker.

label: TB admissions per 1000
rationale: TB = 6-month+ regimen: chronic-duration infectious disease with assured repeat dispensing; small acute weight for initial presentation.

label: Asthma/COPD admissions per 1000
rationale: Chronic respiratory burden (inhalers maintenance therapy) with acute-exacerbation episodes - weighted in both segments.

label: Cancer incidence (crude per 100k - state)
rationale: The DIRECT oncology burden signal the chronic index previously lacked (oncology was only implicit in screening_uptake_pct and DM/MCh superspec depth). Oncology is a high-value chronic therapy area (long-course systemic therapy, targeted/immuno agents, supportive care). Source: ICMR-NCDIR National Cancer Registry Programme state/UT-wise ESTIMATED incidence (data.gov.in, both sexes/all sites; 2022 national total 1,461,427 matches the published NCRP figure), converted to a crude RATE = state cases / state pop_ghs_2025 x 1e5 and assigned FLAT within state. Chronic-only (w 2/3/0): cancer is not an acute first-contact market. STATE resolution is a deliberate, documented limitation - India has no official district-level cancer incidence (the ~30 NCRP PBCRs are city/select-district and populous states e.g. UP/Bihar have none), so a state anchor is the honest ceiling; weight held to 3 (not 5 like measured diabetes/hypertension) because of that coarseness. Within-state oncology texture is carried by the district-level tobacco_use_pct gradient (oral/lung cancer is India's tobacco-driven leading site). Cases/population (not the population-dominated case COUNT) recovers the true per-capita gradient - Kerala 164 and Mizoram 139 highest (documented highest-incidence geographies), young UP/Bihar/Arunachal lowest. Added v1.4.13.

label: Child diarrhoea 2-wk prevalence (%)
rationale: Flagship acute paediatric indication (ORS zinc antibiotics). Two-week recall prevalence = episodic incidence proxy.

label: Child ARI 2-wk prevalence (%)
rationale: Acute respiratory infection in under-5s: antibiotic/antipyretic core of the acute market.

label: Child anaemia (%)
rationale: Paediatric nutritional deficiency - syrups/drops segment; part-programmatic (free IFA) hence moderate weight.

label: Child undernutrition (mean of stunted/wasted/underweight %)
rationale: Undernourished children have higher infection frequency/severity - multiplies acute episode volume; averaged to one anthropometric signal.

label: Malaria+dengue positives per 1000
rationale: Confirmed vector-borne caseload: seasonal acute spikes (antimalarials antipyretics IV fluids platelet support). Summed lab-confirmed positives.

label: Typhoid+diarrhoea admissions per 1000
rationale: Severe enteric infection admissions - water/food-borne acute demand (antibiotics fluids).

label: Child diarrhoea+URI treated per 1000
rationale: Revealed paediatric acute treatment volume in public facilities; complements NFHS prevalence with facility-load data.

label: Snakebite emergencies per 1000
rationale: Rural emergency-care marker (anti-venom cold chain); proxies deep-rural acute reach requirements.

label: Ambient PM2.5 (annual mean)
rationale: Air-pollution load drives ARI/asthma/COPD exacerbations (acute) and long-run respiratory disease (some chronic weight). Satellite-derived: novel-data differentiation.

label: Households without improved sanitation (%)
rationale: Poor sanitation = enteric/parasitic infection risk environment. Stored as 100-improved so higher = more acute-market risk; direction handled in construction.

label: Households without improved water (%)
rationale: Unsafe water = water-borne disease exposure; same construction as sanitation. v1.4.11: acute weight raised 3->4 to match poor_sanitation_pct - enteric disease (diarrhoea/typhoid) is the top acute-paediatric indication and unsafe water is its primary transmission route.

label: Solid cooking-fuel households (% - household air pollution)
rationale: Household air pollution from solid cooking fuel (100 - clean_fuel_pct): a WHO-established leading driver of childhood acute respiratory infection/pneumonia - the antibiotic/antipyretic core of the acute paediatric market. Complements ambient pm25_mean (outdoor) and measured ari_child_pct with the indoor-smoke exposure that hits under-5s hardest. Same NFHS #10 source as the growth-side clean_fuel_pct but opposite construct and sign (parallel to pop_under15_pct vs ageing_transition): a clean-fuel-rich district scores higher on growth AND lower on acute burden - the correct real-world relationship. Direction -1/flip100 documents raw polarity; the flip is applied in build_features. Added v1.4.11.

label: Sub-centres+PHCs per 100k
rationale: First-contact public network where acute episodes present and are prescribed. HWC-reclassified units included for 2019 comparability. Low chronic weight: chronic scripts concentrate higher up the pyramid.

label: CHCs per 100k
rationale: Secondary tier with specialists (referral point where chronic diagnosis often starts; also acute inpatient care) - balanced weight.

label: SDH+DH per 100k
rationale: District/sub-divisional hospitals anchor diagnosis + institutional prescribing; strongest public-infrastructure signal for sustained therapy.

label: OSM hospitals per 100k
rationale: Current-vintage hospital density including the PRIVATE hospitals no census/RHS column carries - and India pharma is ~70% private-market. OSM mapping is urban-biased, so this is a percentile presence/density signal, never a universe count. Chronic over acute: hospitals anchor specialist prescription initiation.

label: OSM clinics & doctors per 100k
rationale: First-contact private clinics / GP practices: the entry point of the acute prescription (fever infection GI) and the referral source for chronic diagnosis. Acute-weighted because episodic illness is treated at the nearest clinic not a hospital.

label: Private share of PM-JAY empanelled hospitals (%)
rationale: Revealed private-market viability: private hospitals empanel only where insured volumes are commercially attractive so a high private share marks districts whose private provision - pharma's main detailing target - is vibrant and open to funded patients. Share (not count) keeps it orthogonal to the density features. NaN where no hospital is empanelled (imputation ladder documents it); also masked to NaN in WB/Odisha/Delhi whose platform picture is structurally partial (v1.4.6).

label: Private medical facilities per 100k (towns 2011)
rationale: EXCLUDED (superseded 2026-07-16): replaced by the osm_* POI family - same private-supply construct but current-vintage OSM vs towns-directory 2011 (was our single biggest data weakness). Documented fallback: re-enable if OSM proves too sparse in a region.

label: MBBS seats per 100k
rationale: Physician pipeline + teaching-hospital service capacity; med-college districts anchor prescriber ecosystems.

label: PG (MD/MS) seats per 100k
rationale: Specialist pipeline: chronic therapy is specialist-initiated (cardiologist endocrinologist) so PG depth is a core chronic addressability signal.

label: DM/MCh super-specialty seats per 100k
rationale: Tertiary referral depth (DM/MCh = cardiology neurology oncology surgical superspecialties). Marks referral-pull hub districts that capture surrounding chronic demand.

label: Medical college hub score (log colleges)
rationale: Count of teaching institutions = institutional gravity/KOL presence beyond seat numbers; log to damp metro pile-up.

label: Total OPD visits per 1000
rationale: Revealed overall care-seeking volume - the single best flow measure of a district's treatable demand actually presenting; skews acute (episodic visits dominate OPD).

label: Acute caseload seasonality (peak-quarter share of annual %)
rationale: Seasonal CONCENTRATION of the episodic acute caseload: share of the FY2018-19 year's malaria/dengue/enteric/child-acute/snakebite volume landing in the district's peak 3-month window (25 = flat year, 100 = single-quarter market), from HMIS-portal monthly data. Spiky districts are the archetypal acute market - monsoon/winter surges that reward seasonal stocking, pre-season detailing and surge distribution; flat districts consume steadily. Complements the annual LEVEL features with SHAPE; guarded (OPD reported >=11/12 months, basket >=120 cases/yr, else NaN -> ladder). Family hmis_monthly, deliberately outside the 13-feature hmis state-reporting sensitivity blend: a within-district shape ratio is far less exposed to state completeness than levels are. Single-FY estimate, read as a relative percentile.

label: Total admissions per 1000
rationale: Hospitalisation throughput = functioning inpatient system (acute severity + chronic complications both flow through IPD).

label: Lab tests per 1000
rationale: Diagnostic activity precedes chronic diagnosis (HbA1c lipid panels): the closest thing we hold to diagnosis capacity in use. Chronic-critical.

label: OSM diagnostic labs per 100k
rationale: Private diagnostics presence (incl. sample-collection points of chain labs): HbA1c/lipid testing that initiates chronic therapy happens largely outside the public HMIS labs we measure in lab_tests_per1000. Chronic-critical, near-zero acute role.

label: Institutional births (%)
rationale: System trust + physical access proxy: where women deliver in facilities, families use formal care for acute episodes too. HMIS deliveries duplicate this - NFHS kept (cleaner denominator).

label: Children fully immunised (%)
rationale: Preventive-care completion = outreach reach + parental engagement with formal medicine; paediatric/acute-aligned.

label: Child acute episodes taken to a provider (%)
rationale: Treatment-seeking CONVERSION for paediatric acute episodes (NFHS-5 #64 diarrhoea + #66 fever/ARI taken to a facility/provider, averaged): burden only monetises where families act on symptoms - separates high-burden-high-conversion acute markets from high-burden-untreated ones. Complements institutional births/immunisation (general formal-care habit) with episode-level acute behaviour. Factsheet suppresses small episode cells: 551/785 observed, missing skews to LOW-burden districts (TN/MP) so the state-median ladder is conservative; moderate weight for 2-week-recall noise.

label: Chronic NCD treatment-realisation rate (%)
rationale: The chronic analog of child_acute_careseek_pct: how well latent chronic (NCD) need CONVERTS into sustained, effective treatment - the market-realisation dimension the index otherwise lacked (burden and OPD volume were carried; conversion was not). DERIVED from NFHS-5 district factsheets, which publish no standalone treated-share indicator but do give both the measured-high biomarker prevalence AND a composite 'measured-high OR taking medicine to control it' for each of diabetes (women: #86 high + #87 very-high vs #88 composite) and hypertension (#92 mild + #93 mod/severe vs #94 composite). composite - measured = the share on medication whose biomarker is now CONTROLLED (they read normal, so enter only via 'taking medicine'); summed over both conditions and divided by the composite NCD pool (88+94), x100 = the realisation RATE. Chronic-only (w 2/3/0): a diabetes/hypertension continuity signal, not an acute first-contact one. INDEPENDENT of the HMIS OPD-visit stream (household-survey biomarker + self-report, not facility throughput) - this is exactly why it succeeds where the held-data OPD-ratio proxy was REJECTED at rho 0.94-0.96: here max rho vs any scored chronic feature is ~0.49 (csection_pct), passing the redundancy gate with wide daylight. Burden-normalised (a ratio, not a level) so it adds conversion, not a second burden count. Weight 3 (not 5): a difference of two survey percentages carries some noise, and the treated-and-CONTROLLED numerator undercounts uncontrolled-on-treatment patients (a conservative, monotone realisation proxy). Direction +: established treatment-realisation = a market that reliably converts diagnosis into repeat chronic prescriptions = more addressable TODAY (headroom/saturation is a separate growth question the index keeps distinct). 783/785 observed. Added v1.4.13.

label: C-section deliveries (%)
rationale: Surgical capacity + private obstetric activity proxy; correlates with higher-value private healthcare consumption.

label: Cancer screening uptake (mean cervical/breast/oral %)
rationale: Early-detection behaviour = diagnosed-chronic pipeline (oncology cardio-metabolic follow-on). Purely chronic-side.

label: Households with health insurance (%)
rationale: Payer coverage sustains multi-year chronic therapy adherence and hospital episodes; the demand side of insurance - pairs with pmjay_hospitals_per100k (the supply side).

label: PM-JAY empanelled hospitals per 100k
rationale: Cashless-care supply: where the ~58-crore-beneficiary PM-JAY scheme has deep empanelment, secondary/tertiary treatment is FUNDED - converting covered households into an effectively paying patient pool. Chronic over acute: PM-JAY claims skew to chronic procedure packages (cardiac oncology dialysis). Caveat: West Bengal (own scheme outside the portal) and 2025 joiners Odisha/Delhi measure platform membership rather than insured supply, so the feature is masked to NaN for those three states in build_features (v1.4.6) - the imputation ladder scores them neutral instead of bottom-decile.

label: Relative Wealth Index (Meta)
rationale: Micro-estimated household wealth: direct ability-to-pay for OOP-dominated Indian pharma. Novel-data differentiation with all-India coverage.

label: Bank deposits per capita (log10 Rs)
rationale: Financial wealth stock per head (RBI 4A current-vintage): savings buffer that funds sustained chronic treatment; log for heavy metro skew.

label: Bank outlets per 100k
rationale: Formal-finance physical reach: enables cashless payment trade credit and distributor banking - channel hygiene for pharma operations.

label: Jan Aushadhi kendras per 100k
rationale: Generic pharmacy channel density: dispensing points + price-sensitive demand marker; also competitive-intensity signal for branded generics. v1.4.11: acute-tilted (4 vs chronic 3) - the retail counter is the acute market's first contact (India's acute demand is OTC/self-medication-first, patient describes symptoms at the chemist), whereas chronic is prescription-and-refill-led. A complete public registry, so it carries the acute bump more safely than under-mapped OSM.

label: OSM retail pharmacies per 100k
rationale: The actual branded-dispensing channel (retail chemists) - previously unobserved; Jan Aushadhi covers only the public generic channel. v1.4.11: acute-tilted (5 vs chronic 3) - India's acute market is OTC/self-medication-first (walk to the chemist, describe symptoms, buy), whereas chronic dispensing is prescription-and-refill-led at a stable pharmacy. OSM under-mapping (~8k mapped of ~0.9M real chemists) means density signal only - the acute weight is 5 not 6-equivalent-max precisely to avoid amplifying urban mapping bias; the complete Jan Aushadhi registry carries the parallel acute bump.

label: Rural salaried-household share (%)
rationale: Salaried households have predictable income - supports monthly chronic refill purchases in rural markets. No team-table equivalent for the SHRUG gap states (all Kerala/Lakshadweep NaN) - lands on the imputation ladder there (v1.4.7 audit).

label: Rural households earning 10k+ (%)
rationale: Premium rural affordability tier: candidates for branded/newer chronic molecules rather than lowest-cost generics. SHRUG gap (157 districts incl. all Kerala/Lakshadweep) backfilled from the team SECC income-band table; scale-calibrated on the 614-district overlap (v1.4.7).

label: Rural vehicle-owning households (%)
rationale: Asset-based affluence + physical mobility to reach chemists/facilities; secondary to RWI hence low weight. 2011 ownership STOCK - the current-vintage registration FLOW side is carried by the vahan family (vehicle_reg_per1000 etc.). No team-table equivalent for the SHRUG gap states (all Kerala/Lakshadweep NaN) - lands on the imputation ladder there (v1.4.7 audit).

label: Work participation rate (%)
rationale: Earning-population share: weak generic affordability signal kept at minimal weight.

label: OOP spend on public delivery (Rs)
rationale: Ambiguous by design: high OOP = burden BUT also demonstrated willingness/capacity to spend on health - and Indian pharma is OOP-funded. Kept positive at low weight; sensitivity-tested.

label: Nightlights intensity (log VIIRS mean)
rationale: Current economic activity level from satellite: cash in the local economy. Novel differentiator; log for metro skew.

label: Rural Kisan credit card share (%)
rationale: Rural formal-credit access smooths lumpy health spending; minor supplementary signal. SHRUG gap (157 districts incl. all Kerala/Lakshadweep) backfilled from the team SECC land-ownership table; scale-calibrated on the overlap (v1.4.7).

label: Deposit growth 3-yr CAGR (%)
rationale: Wealth accumulation MOMENTUM (2023-2026 actuals): districts getting richer will afford more/premium therapy tomorrow.

label: Credit growth 3-yr CAGR (%)
rationale: Credit expansion = business formation/investment appetite - forward commercial vitality.

label: Nightlights annual CAGR (%)
rationale: Satellite-measured economic growth - the flagship forward-looking novel signal, independent of any survey.

label: Credit-deposit ratio (%)
rationale: High CD ratio = local savings deployed locally as credit - entrepreneurial economies that convert wealth into activity.

label: Non-farm jobs per 1000 (EC 2013)
rationale: Structural modernisation: non-farm employment shifts populations toward urban lifestyles chronic risk and formal healthcare.

label: Services employment share (EC 2013)
rationale: Service-economy share: white-collar transition marker (sedentary work - metabolic risk - insurance jobs).

label: Vehicle registrations per 1000 (CY2023)
rationale: Revealed discretionary spending powering out-of-pocket pharma (~50% of Indian drug spend): a household that registers a vehicle this year can fund a prescription this year. CURRENT-vintage flow (CY2023 VAHAN, dump-rows cleaned + FADA-anchor-validated) vs the 2011 SECC ownership STOCK - this is how the framework improves on census-era affordability practice. Telangana/Lakshadweep were not on VAHAN in-window: NaN -> ladder, documented not zeroed.

label: Four-wheeler share of personal registrations (%)
rationale: Premium-affluence MIX: cars vs two-wheelers within the same district's registrations. Being a ratio it needs no population denominator, so district-population error cannot distort it -- but it does need a VOLUME floor: computed only where the district registers >= 200 personal vehicles a year, because below that the mix is noise (3 cars and 0 bikes is not "100% premium"), which otherwise handed ~25 remote hill districts a top-percentile affluence score. High 4W share marks private-pay depth for premium/branded chronic therapy (chronic 4 > acute 2: acute volume is mass-market, chronic-brand economics follow affluence).

label: Vehicle registration growth 2019-2023 (%)
rationale: Consumption momentum through COVID: districts whose registrations regrew past the 2019 pre-COVID base have demand engines (income + credit + aspiration) that also expand pharma spend. Computed only where the 2019 base >= 500 (a new RTO opening mid-window shifts volume between districts and fakes growth); segment-neutral 3/3/3.

label: Graduate share (mean rural+urban %)
rationale: Education drives health literacy diagnosis-seeking and therapy adherence; graduates adopt preventive chronic care earliest. SHRUG gap (158-171 districts incl. all Kerala/Lakshadweep) backfilled from the team SECC education tables; scale-calibrated on the ~600-district overlap (v1.4.7).

label: Women with 10+ yrs schooling (%)
rationale: Women are household health decision-makers: female education is the strongest single predictor of formal healthcare adoption.

label: Clean cooking fuel (%)
rationale: Household modernisation rung strongly associated with rising consumer spending. v1.4.11: acute weight dropped 1->0 - clean fuel is a POSITIVE development/growth signal, but the household-air-pollution ACUTE burden runs the OTHER way (solid-fuel smoke drives childhood ARI), so that construct is now carried with the correct sign by solid_fuel_ari_pct in need/acute_burden rather than as a muddy positive here.

label: Public facility growth 2012-19 (%)
rationale: Public-infrastructure expansion momentum: where the state is adding facilities access is improving - future addressability. v1.4.12: computed only on core components observed in BOTH years (RHS-2012 publishes Kerala CHCs / Uttarakhand SCs+CHCs / Puducherry SCs+PHCs only in the state Total row - a plain row total fabricated tiny baselines, Puducherry +4150%); 2019 HWCs join only with their matched parent component; baselines <10 facilities -> NaN (tiny-base growth is noise; 733/785 observed).

label: Obesity change NFHS4-5 (pp)
rationale: Lifestyle-transition VELOCITY: districts where obesity is rising fastest are tomorrow's diabetes/CVD markets - the chronic future-demand signal.

label: Insurance coverage change NFHS4-5 (pp)
rationale: Payer expansion velocity (largely PM-JAY rollout): rapidly-insuring districts unlock previously unaffordable therapy volume.

label: Full immunisation change NFHS4-5 (pp)
rationale: Outreach-system improvement velocity - formal-care habit formation in the next generation of parents (acute-aligned).

label: Institutional births change NFHS4-5 (pp)
rationale: Facility-trust momentum: households switching into formal care.

label: Ageing shift: decline in under-15 share NFHS4-5 (pp)
rationale: Demographic transition speed: a falling child share = ageing pipeline = growing chronic patient pool. Sign-flipped so faster ageing scores higher; zero acute weight (its acute effect is contractionary).

label: Sanitation improvement NFHS4-5 (pp)
rationale: Development momentum marker. Note the two-sided effect: improving sanitation raises spending power/formal-care use but ERODES future enteric acute burden - hence acute weight 0.

label: Population growth 2015-2025 (%)
rationale: Demographic momentum: where the patient pool itself is expanding (in-migration + natural growth) tomorrow's market outgrows today's rank. Growth skews young/working-migrant -> acute-leaning; chronic prevalence follows with a lag. Same-source 2015 vs 2025 GHS-POP epochs (no census-vs-model level mixing); subnational projection detail mutes but does not misdirect the signal.

label: Census 2011 raw PCA counts (80+ columns)
rationale: EXCLUDED (inputs not features): raw gender-split counts already distilled into density/worker_rate/log_pop; scoring them alongside derived rates would double-count population.

label: Literacy rate (Census 2011)
rationale: EXCLUDED (duplicate): superseded by women_10yr_school_pct (NFHS 2019-21 - fresher and 785-complete vs 640).

label: Under-6 share (Census 2011)
rationale: EXCLUDED (duplicate): superseded by pop_under15_pct (NFHS 2019-21; fuller coverage).

label: Women literate (%)
rationale: EXCLUDED (duplicate): near-collinear with women_10yr_school_pct; one education signal per source retained.

label: Female schooling (%)
rationale: EXCLUDED (duplicate): same construct as women_10yr_school_pct.

label: Household electricity (%)
rationale: EXCLUDED (saturated): near-universal by NFHS-5 - no discriminating power across districts.

label: Sex ratio
rationale: EXCLUDED (relevance): social indicator without a defensible direction for market attractiveness.

label: Women married before 18 (%)
rationale: EXCLUDED (relevance): social-development indicator; no direct pharma-demand channel beyond what education already captures.

label: Institutional deliveries per 1000 (HMIS)
rationale: EXCLUDED (duplicate): NFHS institutional_births_pct kept - survey denominator cleaner than HMIS volume/pop2011.

label: Village-directory 2011 facility/bank columns
rationale: EXCLUDED (superseded): 2011 facility and bank counts replaced by RHS 2019 and RBI DBIE current-vintage equivalents. Exception: pc11_td_medical_priv retained (no current private-infra substitute).

label: IPD malaria/dengue per 1000
rationale: EXCLUDED (double-count): lab-confirmed positives already carry the vector-borne signal; admissions for the same diseases would count them twice.

label: Standalone SECC crosswalk files
rationale: EXCLUDED (duplicate source): per crosswalk README - standalone SECC duplicates the district_frame seccR_/seccU_ modules used here; one source per feature.

label: Walled-off state-apportioned infra estimate
rationale: EXCLUDED (modelled estimate): by team decision this file never enters the index - within a state it is facility_count x state-average so it adds zero district signal beyond facility counts already registered and would double-weight them.

label: HMIS facility counts
rationale: EXCLUDED (duplicate): facility counts taken from RHS data.gov.in panel (longer series reconciled totals); HMIS kept for service volumes only.

label: Rural house ownership (%)
rationale: EXCLUDED (relevance): near-universal rural ownership; no affordability discrimination beyond RWI/income bands.

label: Rural land ownership (%)
rationale: EXCLUDED (relevance): land ownership does not separate health spending power once income-band and salaried shares are in.

label: SECC SC/ST shares
rationale: EXCLUDED (relevance/ethics): demographic composition is not a market-attractiveness variable; deprivation is already captured through income education and wealth measures.

label: EC13 remaining employment columns
rationale: EXCLUDED (redundant): nonfarm_emp_per_1k + services_emp_share carry the structural signal; remaining EC13 splits are near-collinear with them.

label: Children with diarrhoea receiving ORS/zinc (%)
rationale: EXCLUDED (programme-supply artifact): ORS/zinc receipt measures free public-programme distribution reach, not market behaviour - the behavioural conversion signal is carried by child_acute_careseek_pct (episodes taken to a provider). Scoring both would double-count the same episodes.

label: Under-5 / infant mortality rate
rationale: EXCLUDED (no official district source + construct confound): NFHS-5 publishes IMR/U5MR only at STATE level (district mortality samples too small); district U5MR exists only as academic model-based estimates, and wiring one would break the official-sources-only replicability principle. Conceptually U5MR ~ burden x (1 - access) - the product of the two pillars the framework deliberately separates - and its treatable drivers (diarrhoea, ARI, undernutrition, anaemia, unsafe water) are each scored directly; mortality would add access-confounded noise, not market signal.

label: Census 2011 slum population share
rationale: EXCLUDED (notification artifact + unallocatable geography): acquired and bias-gated (town->district via the PC11 town directory; TOT_P reconciles to India 65,494,604 exactly, 0 towns unmatched) but fails construct validity - the PM-JAY/HFR artifact class. State slum shares track what states NOTIFY as slums, not crowding: Bihar 1.2% vs Telangana 13.1% while Bihar's poor-sanitation is 50.5% vs 25.4%; district rho vs poor_sanitation_pct is NEGATIVE (-0.13) and vs density only +0.12 - acute-weighting it would re-depress the same under-notifying eastern belt the v1.4.6 PM-JAY mask repaired.
